label: early input z (positions 1-3) or f at position 2
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase (98% of mass), at steps 1-3, and mostly at step 2 (78% of mass). Token z drives it: z input at steps 1-3 (z at step 2 is 100% precise and is the strongest, about 0.6-1.0 of max). The weaker driver is f at step 2. Within z firings, z at step 2 is much stronger than z at step 1 (around 0.1-0.15 of max). The weakest firings are b, e or q at step 2, and a small copy-phase tail when re-emitting the third token. It never fires at step 0, on the delimiter, or at step 4 or later in the original phase, and is essentially silent during the copy phase. On dev, P 0.80 / R 0.82 / F1 0.81 / mass recall 0.93.

issues: Precision of the z branch is uneven by position. z at t=2 has precision 1.0 and carries 53% of the mass, but z at t=1 (P 0.66, 7% of mass) and z at t=3 (P 0.65, 13% of mass) are weak firings near the threshold. They account for most of the false positives. Precision rises somewhat when the previous token is a vowel or digit, but no clean rule separating fired from silent z at t=1 or t=3 turned up.
f at t=2 has precision 0.88 and 20% of the mass, which is consistent with the claim. f at t=3 (P 0.07) and f at t=1 (P 0) confirm that the f response is specific to position 2.

The small leftover classes are b at t=2 (P 0.29, 3% of mass), e at t=2 (P 0.11) and a copy-phase tail at L=3, recall_idx 2 (P 0.12, 1.8% of mass). The explanation already discloses all three. Adding b at t=2 lowers test F1 from 0.811 to 0.784.
Minor overclaim: the label says 'z at positions 1-3' as if all three were equal, while the effect is strongly concentrated at position 2. The explanation does state this.
skeptic.revised_label: input z at step 2, more weakly at steps 1 and 3, or f at step 2 (original phase)
